results: 1. Complete bedside neurological examination, including cranial nerves, coordination, strength, sensation, reflexes, and plantar responses
bedside eye-movement exam: no ophthalmoplegia and no nystagmus - the classic triad is incomplete
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
2. Observed gait examination with normal walking, tandem walking, heel walking, toe walking, turning, and dual-task/distraction maneuvers
Romberg test: negative - swaying is not worse with the eyes closed
5. Orthostatic blood pressure and pulse measurements
brain MRI: bilateral symmetric hyperintensity in the mammillary bodies, thalami and periaqueductal midbrain, with the LENTIFORM FORK SIGN; reversed after treatment
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: abnormal; bilateral symmetric restricted diffusion in the mammillary bodies, thalami and periaqueductal midbrain
9. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, thyroid-stimulating hormone, vitamin B12, and serum folate
renal and liver function: end-stage renal disease on maintenance haemodialysis
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: abnormal; end-stage renal failure with elevated urea and creatinine
10. Speech and language assessment by a speech-language pathologist
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Nonalcoholic Wernicke encephalopathy due to thiamine deficiency associated with maintenance hemodialysis

ALTERNATIVE 1: Uremic encephalopathy associated with end-stage renal disease

ALTERNATIVE 2: Metabolic encephalopathy related to dialysis-associated thiamine depletion with a lentiform fork sign

ALTERNATIVE 3: Wernicke-like toxic–metabolic encephalopathy from another nutritional or dialysis-related deficiency
